verdict: Avoid for now — Samba pharma/API lending stays on hold until local demand signals turn; only exception is a tightly-structured, invoice-backed facility to an existing, verified Samba unit with full monthly data.
title: Samba Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**An API/formulation unit buys chemical intermediates, runs multi-step synthesis and drying, and sells to formulators or exports; cash is made on yield, solvent recovery and repeat contract volumes, not on price.** Value sits in the customer qualification (a buyer cannot switch a validated supplier quickly), so pricing power is real only where the unit holds an approved vendor status. Working capital is heavy: raw material and solvent inventory plus a long receivable tail. Rating reports on peers show working capital intensity of 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021, down from 77% in FY2018 [9] — so when a proposal lands, check the receivable days and inventory holding against these peer levels; if the unit's intensity is materially above 48%, ask why and demand the ageing.

## What has changed now
**The local demand picture is weak and the national picture is not supportive either.** Jammu and Kashmir GST collections are -10.6% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 16.7 pp slower [D], and electricity demand is -0.5% Apr-to-date against India +9.5%, 10.0 pp slower [D] — both are local stress signals. India-wide output is -2.1% Apr-to-date [D] while bank credit is +21.6% YoY, a gap of +23.7 pp [D], meaning credit is running well ahead of production. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit's own sales growth is real volume or channel stuffing; if growth is claimed without matching power consumption or GST turnover, ask for the returns.**

## Where the growth is — and who to avoid
**Peer results show the opportunity is in API and CDMO capacity, not in plain formulation tolling.** Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA up 84% to Rs. 136 crore and margin at 22.2% from 17.7% [3][5]; RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth and evaluating another acquisition within 12 months [4], though its own Q2 revenue rose 16.5% to Rs. 211.6 crore and the stock fell over 10% [6].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet.** Take monthly GST returns, power bills and stock statements; covenant a minimum EBITDA margin and a receivable-days cap. Rating evidence shows liquidity can swing: Cohance's working capital utilisation fell from 70-90% to 40-50% in Q1FY25 [8], and Concord's high working-capital intensity persisted [9]. **If the unit cannot show monthly GST turnover matching its invoices, ask for the bank statement and reduce the limit.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch power consumption, GST turnover and receivable ageing together — they move before default.** A rating report on a modest-scale peer showed revenue of Rs. 61.0 crore in FY2024 hit by weak US contract research demand, then 35% growth in 7M FY2025 [7]; customer concentration is the recurring risk [7]. **If any two of the three local indicators deteriorate for two quarters, stop new sanctions and review existing limits.**

days beyond peer 48% intensity [9] -> demand collection plan and margin top-up
utilisation above 90% sustained -> restructure limit or seek collateral
